  MINUTES
  VERNON CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 4, 2026
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4305 S. SANTA FE AVENUE

  CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ybarra called the meeting to order at 9:00 a.m.

  FLAG SALUTE
  Mayor Ybarra led the Flag Salute.

  ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:
  Melissa Ybarra, Mayor
  Jesus Rivera, Mayor Pro Tem
  Judith Merlo, Council Member

  ABSENT:
  Crystal Larios, Council Member
  Monica Rodriguez, Council Member

  STAFF PRESENT:
  Brian Saeki, City Administrator
  Zaynah Moussa-Milward, City Attorney
  Genoveva Rocha, City Clerk
  Alice Hui, Finance Director/City Treasurer
  Veronica Petrosyan, Health and Environmental Control Director
  Su Tan, Director of Human Resources
  Robert Sousa, Police Chief
  Dan Wall, Public Works Director-City Engineer
  Todd Dusenberry, Public Utilities General Manager
  Diana Figueroa, Communications and Public Information Manager

  APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Merlo seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called and the motion carried 3-0, Council
  Members Larios and Rodriguez absent.

  PUBLIC COMMENT
  None.

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 2 of 6
  August 4, 2026
  PRESENTATIONS
  1.  Fiscal Year 2025-26 Vernon CommUNITY Fund Scholarship Grant Awards
  Recommendation: A. Receive and file the report on scholarship grants awarded by
  the Vernon CommUNITY Fund (VCF) Grant Committee for Fiscal Year (FY) 2025-
  26; and
  B. Recognize FY 2025-26 VCF Scholarship Grant Recipients for their outstanding
  academic performance, personal achievement, community involvement, and
  leadership.

  Communications & Public Information Manager Figueroa presented the staff
  report.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra called for
  a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Merlo moved and Mayor Pro Tem Rivera seconded a motion to
  approve recommendation A. The question was called and the motion carried 3-0,
  Council Members Larios and Rodriguez absent.

  Mayor Ybarra announced that Communication and Public Information Manager
  Figueroa would continue with recommendation B and introduce the grant
  recipients. Mayor Ybarra then presented the grant recipients with certificates of
  recognition.

  Mayor Ybarra suggested that the Vernon Community Fund Grant Committee
  consider awarding second-year scholarships to students. City Administrator Saeki
  informed the City Council that staff would return with an item to consider providing
  that direction to the committee.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  2.  New Regulations for Vacant Property Registration
  Recommendation: A. Conduct a Public Hearing;
  B. Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) and 15378,
  as an action for which there is no possibility that the ordinance will have any
  significant effect on the environment;
  C. Introduce, read by title only, and waive further reading of Ordinance No. 1314
  establishing Chapter 8.58 (Vacant Property Registration) of Title 8 (Health and
  Safety) of the Vernon Municipal Code pertaining to the mandatory registration and
  regulatory framework for vacant properties; and
  D. Direct staff to schedule adoption for the August 18, 2026, City Council meeting.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 3 of 6
  August 4, 2026
  Mayor Ybarra opened the public hearing at 9:16 a.m. There being none, Mayor
  Ybarra closed the public hearing at 9:17a.m.

  Mayor Ybarra invited further Council discussion. There being none, Mayor Ybarra
  called for a motion.

  City Clerk Rocha read the title of the Ordinance into the record before the roll call
  vote was taken.

  MOTION
  Council Member Merlo moved and Mayor Pro Tem Rivera seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A, B, C, and D. The question was called and the motion
  carried 3-0, Council Member Larios and Rodriguez absent.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Mayor Ybarra inquired if there were any changes to the Consent Calendar. City
  Clerk Rocha announced a correction to the July 21, 2026, meeting minutes, item
  No. 5 – Warrant Register recommendation. She informed the City Council that
  each member received a revised set of meeting minutes with the required
  revisions.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra called for
  a motion to approve the consent calendar.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Merlo seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar with the recommended edits. The question was
  called and the motion carried 3-0, Council Members Larios and Rodriguez absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  3.  Meeting Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the July 21, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
  Minutes.
  4.  Claims Against the City
  Recommendation: Receive and file the claim submitted by Lorenzo Rodriguez
  Luna.
  5.  Operating Account Warrant Register
  Recommendation: Approve Operating Account Warrant Register No. 178, for the
  period of June 14, 2026 through July 4, 2026, totaling $14,167,830.82 and
  consisting of ratification of electronic payments totaling $13,791,033.00 and
  ratification of the issuance of early checks totaling $376,797.82.
  6.  Redevelopment Agency Obligation Retirement Account Warrant Register
  Recommendation: Approve Redevelopment Agency Obligation Retirement
  Account Warrant Register No. 74, for the period of October 19, 2025 through July
  4, 2026 and consisting of ratification of electronic payments totaling $2,250.

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 4 of 6
  August 4, 2026
  7.  Public Works Department Monthly Report
  Recommendation: Receive and file the June 2026 Building Report.
  8.  Amendment No. 1 to Services Agreement with Actum-E, LLC
  Recommendation: A. Find that it is in the best interests of the City to extend the
  agreement with Actum-E, LLC without a competitive selection process, pursuant
  to Vernon Municipal Code Section 3.32.110(B)(2); and
  B. Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute Amendment No. 1 to
  the Services Agreement with Actum-E, LLC, in substantially the same form as
  submitted, extending the term of the agreement for six (6) months for a total
  amount of $38,625, to continue to provide government affairs services related to
  “The BIG 4” cities’ efforts, and bringing the contract total not-to-exceed amount to
  $83,625.
  9.  Quarterly Report of Cash and Investments
  Recommendation: Receive and file the Second Quarter Cash and Investments
  Report
  10.  Professional Services Agreement with All City Management Services Inc. for
  Crossing Guard Services
  Recommendation: Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute a
  Professional Services Agreement with All City Management Services Inc. in
  substantially the same form as submitted, for crossing guard services, for a total
  amount not-to-exceed $179,675, for a three-year term.
  11.  Purchase Order with Merrimac Energy Group for Fuel Procurement
  Recommendation: Approve and authorize issuance of a Purchase Order with
  Merrimac Petroleum, Inc. dba Merrimac Energy Group in an amount not-to-exceed
  $750,000 to procure fuel for the Citywide fleet for Fiscal Year 2026-2027.
  12.  Purchase Order with Quinn Company CAT Retailer
  Recommendation: A. Approve and authorize the issuance of a Purchase Order
  with Quinn Company CAT Retailer (Quinn CAT) for a new Towmaster T-12DT
  Trailer for a total amount not-to-exceed $20,175.24;
  B. Authorize a contingency amount of ten percent (10%) or $2,017.52 for the trailer
  purchase in case of unforeseen fluctuations in price driven by inflation or supply
  chain issues; and
  C. Authorize the City Administrator to facilitate the bidding and purchase of a
  comparable utility trailer for an amount not-to-exceed $22,192.76 (Quinn CAT price
  plus contingency amount) from an alternate source/dealership should Quinn CAT
  availability be impacted by inventory shortages.
  13.  Sewer System Management Plan Update
  Recommendation: A. Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California
  Environmentally Quality Act (CEQA) in accordance with the common-sense
  exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3), because it can be seen
  with certainty that there is no possibility that the activity in question may have a
  significant effect on the environment; and
  B. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-036 approving and adopting the updated Sewer
  System Management Plan (SSMP) and authorizing the Legally Responsible
  Official to certify and submit the SSMP to the California State Water Resources
  Control Board (SWRCB).

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 5 of 6
  August 4, 2026
  14.  Report on Emergency Sewer Repairs for City Housing Approved by the City
  Administrator
  Recommendation: Receive and file the report regarding emergency sewer main
  line repairs affecting City-owned housing completed by Quality Jet Rooter, Inc., as
  approved by the City Administrator pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Section
  3.32.250.
  15.  Fiscal Year 2026-27 Membership Dues for California Municipal Utilities
  Association
  Recommendation: Approve and authorize the issuance of a payment to the
  California Municipal Utilities Association (CMUA) for the annual membership dues
  for fiscal year 2026-27 for a total amount not-to-exceed $116,572.

  NEW BUSINESS

  16.  Participation in a Multiple Employer Other Post-Employment Benefits
  (OPEB)/Pension Section 115 Trust and Approval of Related Agreements with
  Global Retirement Partners, LLC d/b/a Shuster Advisory Group
  Recommendation:
  A. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-037 Approving the Multiple Employer
  OPEB/Pension Section 115 Trust administered by Shuster Advisory Group, LLC,
  for the purpose of pre-funding the City’s pension and OPEB obligations; and
  authorizing the transfer of the City’s current OPEB trust from the California
  Employers’ Retiree Benefit Trust (CERBT) administered by CalPERS; and
  B. Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute the Trust Adoption
  Agreement for participation in the Multiple Employer OPEB/Pension Section 115
  Trust and the related Investment Advisor Agreement with Global Retirement
  Partners, LLC, d/b/a Shuster Advisory Group, a HUB International Company
  (SHUSTER) and the Trust Administrative Services Agreement with Shuster
  Advisory Group, LLC, in substantially the same form as submitted.

  Finance Director Hui presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra called for
  a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Merlo moved and Mayor Pro Tem Rivera seconded a motion to
  approve recommendation A and B. The question was called and the motion carried
  3-0, Council Members Larios and Rodriguez absent.

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 6 of 6
  August 4, 2026
  ORAL REPORTS
  17.  City Administrator Reports on Activities and Other Announcements

  City Administrator Saeki announced National Night Out event taking place later in
  the evening on the City Hall lawn. He also provided details for the Southern
  California Air Quality Management District Hearing Board on August 5, 2026
  regarding Lineage Logistics, and announced that the Vernon CommUNITY Fund
  is accepting nonprofit applications. Lastly, he spoke about the upcoming American
  Red Cross Blood Drive on August 13, 2026, and commented on the completion of
  the Southeast Community Foundation tutoring program.
  18.  Council Reports on Activities (including AB 1234), Announcements, or
  Directives to Staff
  None.
  CLOSED SESSION
  At 9:23 a.m., Mayor Ybarra recessed the meeting to Closed Session
  19.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Simon Perez Melchor v. City of Vernon, et al.
  Los Angeles Superior Court Case No. 24NWCV01639

  RECONVENE
  At 9:47 a.m., Mayor Ybarra adjourned the Closed Session and reconvened the
  regular meeting.
  CLOSED SESSION REPORT
  City Attorney Moussa-Milward reported that the City Council met in Closed
  Session, discussed the item on the agenda, and took no reportable action.
  ADJOURNMENT
  Mayor Ybarra adjourned the meeting at 9:47 a.m.

  _____________________________
  MELISSA YBARRA, Mayor
